Env: dev  
Project: (none)

Overall verdict: needs_changes. The implementer’s summary correctly declares `Repo`, `Env: dev`, and `Project: (none)`. Their `target_context.commands_run` contains only pytest commands and no forbidden command shapes.

FINDING (high, correctness): `HeldLedgerLock.authorizes()` can still authorize a forged token when any holder has the sidecar lock, so F002 write mode is not actually bound to the F005-owned held-lock context. Evidence: `invocation_ledger.py:423-426` treats any contended nonblocking flock as authorization, and `authorizes()` at `invocation_ledger.py:478-482` only checks active/path plus “someone holds the lock”; the new test at `test_canonical_backfill_f002.py:412-422` explicitly shows a forged token becoming authorized once a separate `hold_ledger_lock(ledger)` context exists. Recommendation: bind the token to the specific acquired lock context, e.g. a live private lock handle/capability minted by `hold_ledger_lock`, and add a regression where a forged token remains unauthorized while another thread/process holds the sidecar lock.

Checks run:
$ git status --short
$ git diff --stat HEAD~1
$ git diff --name-only HEAD~1
$ git check-ignore .dontpanic/canonical-backfill-evidence.json
$ git ls-files .dontpanic/canonical-backfill-evidence.json
$ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_canonical_backfill_f002.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
$ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECO
